text:
erin: Heads up — we're trying to settle a publish strategy for the JS SDK. Need quick input on conditional exports (node vs edge vs deno), types entrypoints, and auth/retry differences between ESM/CJS. Also seeing onboarding friction in sample apps (Vercel/CF). Any blockers?

ben: saw a crash in the Vercel sample: "http.Agent is not defined" when importing the CJS bundle on their edge runtime.

maya: yup — edge runtimes don't have node http internals. Our current auth layer assumes node Agent + axios in the CJS build. Edge needs a fetch-based implementation.

raul: we should use conditional exports to route edge imports to an ESM fetch-based file and node to either ESM/CJS versions. Something like:
```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/node/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs",
      "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
    }
  },
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
}
```
But note: npm's conditional exports keys are limited; using an "edge" key is not standard — we'd use environment/condition like "browser" or custom bundler flags.

erin: correct — can't invent custom keys. Typical pattern: "node" condition + "browser" for non-node (usable by many bundlers), and then have an explicit entrypoint for workers (e.g., import from 'sdk/edge'). But we want minimal confusion for end users.

sam: another option is to expose a separate package subpath: `@redwood/sdk` (main) and `@redwood/sdk/edge` (explicit edge build). That avoids relying on nonstandard conditions.

maya: +1 for explicit subpath. Cleaner and avoids subtle bundler mismatches. For DX, we should document which import to use in the sample apps and detect at runtime if wrong build is loaded.

ben: typing note — Typescript projects expect a single "types" field. If we have different runtime entrypoints, we should still point "types" at a flattening declarations file (dist/index.d.ts) that re-exports the declarations for edge/node. Avoid putting types conditionally in exports; TS only reads the "types" entry.

raul: if we need different overloads or platform-specific types, use `typesVersions` to map by TS version, but probably unnecessary here. Generating a single umbrella d.ts that delegates platform specifics via overloaded signatures should be fine.

erin: what about retries/auth parity? We currently have axios+retry in node/cjs and fetch+manual-backoff in edge/mjs. Should the API surface be identical (same backoff defaults, jitter, maxRetries)?

ben: yes — keep identical semantics. Implementation can differ. Important: AbortSignal support on edge (for cancel) and proper signal wiring in node. Also ensure error shapes match (so apps can implement the same retry hooks).

maya: minor DX bug: sample app's README instructed users to import `createClient` from the root — that picks CJS on some deployers and crash. We should update sample to `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk/edge'` for Vercel Edge example, or call out platform table.

sam: I'll add CI smoke tests: publish a `canary-sdk` package from the PR build and run the Vercel and Cloudflare sample apps against it. Also add a quick Node 14/16 test for CJS.

raul: build/publish tasks we need: build:node:esm, build:node:cjs, build:edge, build:types, pack:canary. Also update package.json exports to point require->cjs, import->node esm, browser->edge shim (or use explicit subpath).

maya: snippet for package.json we tested locally (works for bundlers that respect "browser"):
```json
{
  "main": "dist/node/index.cjs",
  "module": "dist/node/index.mjs",
  "browser": "dist/edge/index.mjs",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs",
      "import": "./dist/node/index.mjs",
      "default": "./dist/node/index.mjs"
    },
    "./edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
  }
}
```
But reminder: not all bundlers honor "browser" or conditional exports the same way — hence explicit `/edge` subpath is safest.

erin: good tradeoffs. Action items: 1) sam to wire canary publish + sample app smoke tests; 2) maya + ben to split auth impl and surface identical retry API; 3) raul to prepare package.json exports + docs for import table; 4) update sample READMEs to point to explicit edge subpath.

sam: on it. I'll open a PR with the CI job and a canary publish step today.

ben: fyi: add a quick runtime check in the SDK that logs a warning if a CJS build runs in a worker environment (detect lack of process.versions.node and throw a helpful error). Saves a lot of support time.

erin: love that. Also add metrics for how many users pick root vs /edge so we can iterate.

sdk-bot: published canary job triggered by #ci — will post status once PR passes. :robot_face:

maya: thanks — this should remove most onboarding friction. I'll update the Vercel sample README after canary verifies. :+1:

erin: wrapping up — if nobody objects, we'll run the canary this afternoon and collect results tomorrow.

ben: :+1:
maya: :+1:
raul: :+1:
sam: :+1:
